meta.form_update_notice: Effective February 16, 2026, all applications must use the updated Application for a Permit to Construct or Demolish form.
meta.notes: This list is not exhaustive per the City of Toronto. When in doubt, contact Toronto Building at toronto.ca/building or call 311. Zoning By-law compliance is always required regardless of permit status.

common_forms.note: These forms appear on nearly every permit application. They are listed here once for reference and repeated in each rule's required_forms array with context-specific notes.

F-001.name: Application for a Permit to Construct or Demolish
F-001.description: The primary building permit application form. Required for ALL permit submissions. Updated version mandatory as of February 16, 2026.

F-002.name: Schedule 1: Designer Information Form
F-002.description: Required for all designers except Engineers and Architects. Property Owners exempted from Qualification/Certification must complete this form to specify the reason for exemption.

F-003.name: Assumption of Responsibility for Engineering Content Form
F-003.description: Required when permit drawings bear the seal of a professional engineer.

F-004.name: Tree Declaration Form
F-004.description: Required for all projects where there is potential for damage to private or City trees.

F-005.name: Declaration Form – Overhead Electrical Conductors
F-005.description: Required for all new buildings and additions. Confirms compliance with OBC Article 3.1.20.1. Must be signed by the designer.

F-006.name: Prescriptive Energy Efficiency Design Summary Form
F-006.description: Required for new Part 9 residential buildings or additions when using the prescriptive compliance method under OBC Supplemental Standard SB-12.

F-007.name: Performance Compliance Methods Form
F-007.description: Alternative to F-006. Used when complying with energy efficiency requirements via performance or other acceptable compliance methods.

F-008.name: Infill Public Notice Declaration Form
F-008.description: Required for residential infill construction and demolition projects, including additions greater than 100 m².

F-009.name: Plumbing Data Sheet
F-009.description: Required when applying for a plumbing permit related to work on private property or within a building.

F-010.name: Rental Renovation Licence Screening Form
F-010.description: Required for all permits related to repair or renovation of a residential unit. Determines if a rental renovation licence is also required under Toronto Municipal Code Ch. 662.

F-011.name: Consent to Enter – Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program
F-011.description: Required when installing a backwater valve and sump pump together. Allows Toronto Water to verify eligibility for the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program.

always_required_notes: Zoning By-law compliance is required for ALL projects, even those that do not require a building permit.
This list is not exhaustive. When in doubt, contact Toronto Building via toronto.ca/building or call 311.
Even if a building permit is not required, other permits (e.g. electrical, heritage, sign) may still apply.
As the building owner, you are ultimately responsible for complying with all building requirements.
Failure to obtain required permits can result in costly construction delays, legal action, and/or the removal of completed work.
Effective February 16, 2026, all permit applications must use the updated Application for a Permit to Construct or Demolish form.
